name: MediaQuorix – Media Library Health Manager
author: subekshya76

sections.description:
MediaQuorix helps you keep your WordPress Media Library healthy, organized and easier to maintain.

Use MediaQuorix to review your media library, identify potential issues and manage media files from a dedicated administration area.

Features include:

  • Media Health Dashboard: View your media health score, summary cards and key media insights.
  • Media Explorer: Browse and filter media files by file type, upload date, file size, issues and sorting options.
  • Media Scanning: Scan your library to identify potential issues, including unused media, duplicates, large files, oversized images and missing metadata.
  • Issues Hub: Review findings from the latest scan, grouped by issue type, with links to affected media and relevant management screens.
  • Missing Alt Text: Find images with missing alt text, titles or captions and edit available metadata inline.
  • Large Media: Review files by size, identify unusually large files and use the available bulk actions.
  • Media Cleanup: Review frequently used and potentially unused media using the available cleanup tools.
  • Recycle Bin: Browse trashed media by category, restore items and permanently delete files using the available controls.
  • Storage Overview: Review storage usage by file type and access lists of large media files.
  • Settings: Configure available scanning, cleanup, notification and advanced options.
  • Help & Support: Find contextual guidance throughout the administration area.

Designed with safety in mind

Scanning is intended to inspect your media library without modifying the original media files. MediaQuorix provides review and cleanup controls to help you make informed decisions before removing files. Always review the available confirmation options before performing destructive actions.

MediaQuorix is designed to make media library maintenance easier while keeping important management information accessible.

Third-Party Resources

MediaQuorix does not bundle or load any third-party libraries, scripts, fonts or
external services.

Everything shipped with the plugin is part of MediaQuorix and is licensed under
the same license as the plugin, GPL-2.0-or-later:

  • PHP source files (plugin code).
  • admin/css/admin.css and admin/css/explorer.css (stylesheets).
  • admin/js/admin.js and admin/js/explorer.js (scripts).
  • assets/icons/mediacare.svg (plugin icon, a custom SVG graphic).

No external fonts, CDNs, tracking scripts or third-party APIs are contacted at
runtime.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the mediaquorix folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate “MediaQuorix – Media Library Health Manager” in the Plugins screen.
  3. Open MediaQuorix in the admin sidebar to reach the dashboard.
sections.faq:
Does MediaQuorix delete my media files?

No. Scanning reads your library and never modifies, moves or deletes any media.
Cleanup always asks for confirmation first, and folders only store names —
your files stay exactly where they are.

Where are my settings stored?

In a single mediacare_settings option. Scan history is stored in the
{prefix}mediacare_scans table, findings in {prefix}mediacare_issues and
folders in {prefix}mediacare_folders.

Will deactivating the plugin remove my data?

No. Deactivation keeps all settings and history. Data is only removed on
uninstall if you enable “Delete MediaQuorix data when the plugin is uninstalled”
under Settings → MediaQuorix → Advanced.
sections.changelog:
1.7.0

  • The Media Organizer and Media Explorer screens are now a single, focused Media
    Explorer: browse and narrow the library by file type, upload date, file size,
    issue and sort order, and see the results update as you change them.
  • Dashboard Media Insights panel and per-issue review links in the storage
    breakdown, plus an audio bucket, faster media display and a first-run
    onboarding panel.
  • Contextual help snippets on every screen and a broader accessibility pass.
  • Database indexes for scan queries so large libraries stay responsive, with a
    safe automatic upgrade.
  • A dedicated daily maintenance event that enforces the new “keep scan history”
    retention setting and prunes unused file rows automatically.
  • Bulk selection on the Large Media screen so files can be moved to the trash
    straight from any category tab.
  • Large Media now lists every media file by size, largest first, and flags the
    largest 10% of your library (minimum one file once there are at least five)
    against the library average, with a summary of total, average, median and
    largest size plus per-file multipliers and top-percent position. Comparison
    columns are hidden when there are too few files to compare, and the dashboard
    card always shows the real count and combined size.
  • A Recycle Bin screen with category filters (images, video, audio, documents
    and more) to browse trashed media, restore items in bulk, and permanently
    delete them when confirmation is enabled.
  • Orphaned files — anything left in the uploads folder with no Media Library
    entry — are now detected during a scan and reported alongside unused media so
    stray files are easy to review.
  • New Issues hub: every finding from the latest scan in one list, grouped by
    type with counts and reclaimable sizes, each row linking to the affected
    media and the screen that owns the fix.
  • New Missing Alt Text screen: filter images by missing alt text, title or
    caption and fix each field inline without leaving MediaQuorix.
  • Cleanup now shows your Most Frequently Used media and folds unused media in
    as “Potentially Unused Media” with the full removal toolset; the standalone
    Unused Media menu item is gone.
  • Dashboard cards now open the matching screen: Large Media, Missing Alt Text
    and Potential Issues all link straight to real, filtered results.
  • Storage Overview now shows the total at the top and each file-type card links
    straight to the matching Large Media tab, with “Review files” links on the
    breakdown chart.
  • Fixed “Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page” when opening the Large
    Media screen directly.
  • Media Explorer Favorites count now matches the visible list; favorites whose
    file has been trashed are no longer counted.
  • Media Explorer was streamlined down to its filters: the search bar, folder
    management, favorites, smart folders, suggestions, bulk move, bulk favorites,
    bulk metadata editing and bulk trash controls were removed (together with
    their per-item checkboxes and stars) so the screen focuses on finding media.
    Filters still apply automatically as they change.
  • The Issues, Missing Alt Text and Duplicate Media screens stay reachable from
    the links that use them but are hidden from the menu to keep navigation
    focused.
  • Cleanup’s “Most Frequently Used” and “Potentially Unused Media” sections are
    now collapsible, and large sizes show two decimals.
  • The dashboard “Unused Media” count and the health score now ignore stray
    orphaned uploads (for example WebP or resized variants with no Media Library
    record), so the number reflects real unused media. Orphans are still listed
    in the Issues hub.

1.6.0

  • Phase 6: full smart folder rule builder — create and edit smart folders with
    your own rule combinations across ten fields (file name, type, size, upload
    date, title, alt text, caption, health status, usage status and folder),
    with a live one-click preset filler and a dedicated “edit rules” action on
    every smart folder. Every rule list is validated and sanitized server side.

1.5.0

  • Phase 5: Smart Folders in the Media Organizer — ready-made smart views
    (Most Recent, Large Files, Large Images, Potentially Unused, Duplicates,
    Missing Alt Text and Recycle Bin), user-defined smart folders created from
    rule templates, per-user media favorites with a dedicated view, and keyword
    based folder suggestions that can be applied or dismissed.

1.4.0

  • Phase 4: Media Organizer — create, rename and delete folders, browse All
    Media or Unorganized, search and sort, and move items in bulk. Folder
    membership is shown in the Media Explorer and the media viewer.

1.2.0

  • Phase 2 completion: live Storage, Metadata and Reports screens backed by the
    latest completed scan.

1.1.0

  • Phase 2: full media scanning pipeline — usage index, issue detection and media
    health scoring. Media Explorer now filters real results and opens the viewer.

1.0.0

  • Phase 1: plugin foundation, admin navigation, dashboard UI, reusable design
    system, settings, security and database foundation.

upgrade_notice.1.7.0: Adds six composite database indexes on upgrade (tables are updated in place, nothing is recreated) and a daily maintenance event that prunes old scan history according to the new retention setting. No action needed.
upgrade_notice.1.6.0: Smart folder rule editing goes live: existing smart folders keep their current rules, and every smart folder now shows an "edit rules" action. No schema changes — tables from 1.5.0 are reused as-is.
upgrade_notice.1.5.0: Adds Smart Folders: three new tables (smart folders, favorites, suggestions) are created automatically on upgrade; existing media files are untouched. Health based smart views fill in after the next media scan.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Adds the Media Organizer with folders. Two new tables are created on upgrade; existing media files are untouched.
upgrade_notice.1.2.0: Adds live Storage, Metadata and Reports screens. No schema changes; run a media scan once to populate them.
